title: Epic A: Engine core — shared module library, contract v2, single-pass analysis
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Replace ten copy-pasted Bash modules with ten thin producers on top of one shared library (modules/lib/ubs-common.sh) and one stdlib-only Python analysis package (modules/helpers/ubs_core/). Every module then satisfies the same contract (modules/contract.json): identical flags, identical output formats rendered by one renderer, identical suppression semantics (implemented once, at count time), one severity vocabulary, language-prefixed stable category and rule ids, and a fixed process budget (≤ 25 processes per module run instead of hundreds).

## Why this is first
Fixes currently land in one language and never propagate (GH #85 two-tier constant-time vocabulary → Rust only; GH #91 suppression placement → JS only). Measured: the JS module on 407 TypeScript files ran 900 s at ~18% CPU, i.e. the run is dominated by fork/exec and pipe serialisation of per-category `rg | grep | awk | wc | python3` pipelines, not by analysis. The performance (C), parity (D), and new-language (I) workstreams all become cheap once this lands, and impossible to do ten times otherwise.

## Findings record (produced by every module, rendered by one renderer)
{"schema":"ubs.finding/1","lang":"python","rule_id":"py.security.ct-compare","category_id":"python.security","severity":"critical","confidence":0.82,"file":"src/auth.py","line":42,"col":9,"end_line":42,"end_col":31,"message":"Secret compared with ==","remediation":"Use hmac.compare_digest()","fix":{"kind":"replace","range":[42,9,42,31],"text":"hmac.compare_digest(a, b)"},"fingerprint":"sha256:…","suppressed":false,"source":"ast|regex|helper","extras":{}}
fingerprint = sha256(rule_id ‖ relative path ‖ whitespace-and-identifier-normalised statement text ‖ ordinal among identical statements) so it survives line shifts and local renames; emitted as SARIF partialFingerprints.ubs/v1.

## Contract v2 summary
Flags: --format=text|json|jsonl|sarif|toon, --ci, --fail-on-warning, -v, -q, --jobs=N, --files-from=PATH (NUL-separated), --exclude=GLOBS, --exclude-tests, --strict-gitignore, --category=CSV, --skip=CSV, --rules=DIR, --emit-findings-json=PATH, --list-rules, --dump-rules=DIR, --list-categories, --include-ext=CSV, OUTPUT_FILE positional. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings per policy / 2 environment or usage; --list-*/--dump-rules never scan and exit 0. Env: UBS_PROFILE, UBS_CATEGORY_FILTER, UBS_SKIP_TYPE_NARROWING (value 1 only), UBS_VERIFIED_ASSET_DIR, NO_COLOR; LC_ALL=C exported to child tools. Summary keys: language, files, critical, warning, info, categories[], findings[], extras{profile}. Category ids <lang>.<slug>; rule ids <lang>.<area>.<slug>, stable (renames via a rule_aliases table).

## Done when
contract_conformance.py is green for all ten modules, manifest totals are unchanged per ported module (golden-diffed), ubs-java.sh is under 4,000 lines, and UBS_PROFILE reports ≤ 25 processes per module run.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

## Success Criteria
Ten modules pass contract_conformance.py; each module run spawns ≤ 25 processes; manifest totals unchanged per port; ubs-java.sh < 4,000 lines.

title: Epic D: Detector parity and calibration — registry, shared analyzers, FP corpus, confidence
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Every detector family that exists in one language exists in every language where the concept applies, driven by a machine-readable registry (detectors.yml) from which the README coverage matrix is generated and against which the harness asserts fixture pairs. Findings carry a calibrated `confidence`, and the README's false-positive claim (8–12%) is replaced by a measured, nightly-enforced number.

## Evidence of the gap
Constant-time-compare detector exists in 4/10 modules and only Rust has the GH #85 two-tier vocabulary; Python (ubs-python.sh:4315) and Go (ubs-golang.sh:6103) use a flat substring regex that flags `TARGET_SIGS.get(sig) == "asyncio_task"` and `if token == "rm":` as CRITICAL — these are the 9 self-scan false positives. deep_guard exists in 3/10 (js, python, ruby). Type narrowing in 5/10. ast-grep rule packs: rust 77, go 64, python 52, js 37, java 34, cpp 32, ruby 28, csharp 4, swift 1, elixir 0. Taint exists in all 10 but swift/elixir have no provenance path and no module resets taint state at function boundaries. normalize_severity() exists in 1/10 (swift).

## Mechanisms
Registry + generated matrix; shared analyzers in ubs_core (epic A); a monotone-framework taint engine with function summaries (Kildall worklist, Sharir–Pnueli functional summaries) replacing per-language loops; FP corpus of pinned clean OSS repos with stratified (Neyman) sampling; split-conformal per-detector confidence with a marginal coverage guarantee; SPRT-gated nightly budgets; submodular (greedy, ≥ 1−1/e) selection of smoke fixtures per CPU second.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)

title: Fix script_dir() for Homebrew symlink resolution (GH#21)
description:
## Problem

`script_dir()` in `ubs:699` fails when UBS is invoked via Homebrew symlink because macOS `readlink` returns relative paths. The current implementation:

```bash
script_dir(){ local src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; while [ -h "$src" ]; do src="$(readlink "$src")"; done; cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd; }
```

When `readlink` returns a relative path (e.g., `../../Cellar/ubs/1.0/bin/ubs`), the next loop iteration tries to resolve this relative to CWD instead of relative to the symlink's parent directory.

## Root Cause

macOS `readlink` (BSD variant) returns the literal symlink target without canonicalizing. GNU `readlink` on Linux returns an absolute path. The portable fix is to `cd` into the symlink's parent directory before calling `readlink`, so relative paths resolve correctly.

## Implementation Plan

### Fix script_dir() (ubs:699)

Replace the one-liner with the portable pattern:

```bash
script_dir(){
    local src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    while [ -h "$src" ]; do
        local dir="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd)"
        src="$(readlink "$src")"
        # If readlink returned a relative path, resolve against symlink's parent
        [[ "$src" != /* ]] && src="$dir/$src"
    done
    cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd
}
```

Key change: After `readlink`, check if the result is relative (doesn't start with `/`). If so, prepend the symlink's parent directory. This handles chains of relative symlinks correctly.

## Files to Modify

- `ubs` line 699 (script_dir function -- single line to multi-line)

## Usage sites that benefit

- `resolve_module_path()` at ubs:1646-1657 uses `script_dir` to find `modules/ubs-*.sh`
- Git detection at ubs:1860-1866 uses `script_dir` to check for `.git` directory
- Both break when script_dir returns wrong path via Homebrew symlink
acceptance_criteria:
1. `script_dir()` returns correct directory when invoked via Homebrew symlink on macOS
2. `script_dir()` still works when invoked directly (no symlink)
3. `script_dir()` works with chains of relative symlinks (A -> B -> C)
4. `script_dir()` works on Linux (GNU readlink, absolute paths)
5. Module resolution via `resolve_module_path()` finds modules correctly via symlink
6. No bash version requirement change (must work with bash 3.2+ on macOS)
notes:
## E2E Test Script (scripts/test_symlink_resolution.sh)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "=== script_dir() symlink resolution test ==="
PASS=0; FAIL=0

TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
REAL_DIR="$TMPDIR/real/bin"
LINK_DIR="$TMPDIR/links"
mkdir -p "$REAL_DIR" "$LINK_DIR"

# Create a minimal test script that sources script_dir and prints result
cat > "$REAL_DIR/test_script.sh" << 'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
script_dir(){
    local src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    while [ -h "$src" ]; do
        local dir="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd)"
        src="$(readlink "$src")"
        [[ "$src" != /* ]] && src="$dir/$src"
    done

}
echo "$(script_dir)"
SH
chmod +x "$REAL_DIR/test_script.sh"

# Test 1: Direct invocation
RESULT=$("$REAL_DIR/test_script.sh")
[[ "$RESULT" == "$REAL_DIR" ]] && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: direct invocation got '$RESULT' want '$REAL_DIR'"; ((FAIL++)); }

# Test 2: Single relative symlink
ln -sf "../../real/bin/test_script.sh" "$LINK_DIR/test_link"
RESULT=$("$LINK_DIR/test_link")

# Test 3: Absolute symlink
```

title: Feature: Publish toon_rust as library crate to crates.io
description:
## Overview

Publish toon_rust to crates.io as a library crate with both lib and bin targets, enabling Rust projects to use TOON encoding/decoding without spawning a subprocess.

## Background

Currently toon_rust is only available as a binary (`tru`). This works for CLI tools and bash scripts, but Rust projects that want TOON support must:
1. Shell out to the binary (subprocess overhead)
2. Parse stdout/stderr (fragile)
3. Handle binary availability (may not be installed)

A library crate solves all these issues.

## Proposed API

```rust
// lib.rs
pub fn encode(json: &str) -> Result<String, ToonError>;
pub fn encode_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, ToonError>;
pub fn decode(toon: &str) -> Result<String, ToonError>;
pub fn decode_value(toon: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, ToonError>;

// With options
pub fn encode_with_options(json: &str, opts: EncodeOptions) -> Result<String, ToonError>;

pub struct EncodeOptions {
    pub delimiter: Delimiter,      // Comma, Tab, Pipe
    pub indent: usize,             // Default 2
    pub key_folding: KeyFolding,   // Off, Safe
    pub flatten_depth: Option<usize>,
}
```

## Cargo.toml Structure

```toml
[package]
name = "toon"
version = "0.2.0"

[lib]
name = "toon"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "tru"
path = "src/main.rs"
```

## Usage Examples

```rust
use toon::{encode, decode};

let json = r#"{"name": "test", "values": [1, 2, 3]}"#;
let toon_output = encode(json)?;
let roundtrip = decode(&toon_output)?;
assert_eq!(json, roundtrip);
```

## Benefits

1. **No subprocess overhead** - Direct function calls
2. **Type safety** - Rust error handling
3. **Composability** - Use in pipelines, iterators
4. **Testability** - Unit test TOON encoding in Rust projects
5. **Discoverability** - Found via crates.io search

## Migration Path

- Existing binary users: No change (bin target still works)
- New Rust projects: `cargo add toon` and use library API
- UBS: Could optionally include as dependency if rewritten in Rust

## Dependencies

None - can be done independently.

## Notes

This work happens in the toon_rust repository.
Consider whether to rename the crate from `toon_rust` to just `toon`.

title: Pass .ubsignore patterns to bandit via -x flag (GH#22)
description:
## Problem

Bandit ignores .ubsignore patterns because the patterns from GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS are not passed to the bandit invocation. This produces 10,879 false findings from test files and other excluded paths.

## Root Cause

In `modules/ubs-python.sh:2746-2754`, bandit is invoked with `-x "${_EXC:-}"` where `_EXC` is built only from the hardcoded `EXCLUDE_DIRS` array (line 369-370). The `EXTRA_EXCLUDES` from `--exclude=` flag (line 212) gets appended to `EXCLUDE_DIRS` at line 370, but `GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (populated from .ubsignore by `load_ignore_patterns()` in `ubs:57-97`) is only passed to modules via the `--exclude=` argument at `ubs:2024`. The module argument parser at line 212 puts this into `EXTRA_EXCLUDES`, which does get added to `EXCLUDE_DIRS`.

**Wait** -- re-reading the code flow more carefully:
1. `ubs` main script loads .ubsignore into `GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (ubs:57-97)
2. `ubs` passes `--exclude=$GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` to each module (ubs:2024)
3. Module parses `--exclude=*` into `EXTRA_EXCLUDES` (ubs-python.sh:212)
4. `EXTRA_EXCLUDES` gets appended to `EXCLUDE_DIRS` (ubs-python.sh:370)
5. Bandit uses `EXCLUDE_DIRS` to build `-x` argument (ubs-python.sh:2746-2754)

This chain SHOULD work. The bug may be more subtle:
- The patterns in .ubsignore might use glob syntax (`modules/helpers/*.go`) that bandit's `-x` flag doesn't understand (it expects directory paths, not globs)
- Or `apply_ignore_filters()` (ubs:1436-1484) creates a filtered workspace via rsync, but bandit is invoked against the original `PROJECT_DIR` instead of `FILTERED_PROJECT_DIR`

### Likely actual fix

The `apply_ignore_filters()` function at ubs:1436-1484 creates `FILTERED_PROJECT_DIR` and sets `PROJECT_DIR` to it. Bandit (and all other tools) should use this filtered dir. Verify that `PROJECT_DIR` is correctly set to the filtered copy BEFORE modules run. If the filtering fails (no rsync), the patterns need to be converted to bandit-compatible -x paths.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Verify the filter chain (ubs main script)

Check that `apply_ignore_filters()` runs before module dispatch and that `PROJECT_DIR` is updated to `FILTERED_PROJECT_DIR`. If not, move the call earlier.

### 2. Convert glob patterns to directory paths for bandit

Bandit's `-x` flag expects comma-separated directory/file paths, not globs. Add a conversion step in ubs-python.sh before building the bandit command:

```bash
# Convert glob patterns to expanded paths
local -a bandit_excludes=()
for d in "${EXCLUDE_DIRS[@]}"; do
    # If it's a glob, expand it
    if [[ "$d" == *"*"* ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r match; do
            bandit_excludes+=("$match")
        done < <(find "$PROJECT_DIR" -path "$PROJECT_DIR/$d" 2>/dev/null)
    else
        bandit_excludes+=("$d")
    fi
done
```

### 3. Verify with test suite directory

The .ubsignore contains `test-suite/` which is the main source of false positives. After the fix, `bandit -q -r "$PROJECT_DIR" -x "test-suite"` should skip all files under test-suite/.

## Files to Modify

- `modules/ubs-python.sh` lines 2746-2754 (bandit invocation)
- `ubs` lines 1436-1484 (verify filter chain runs before modules)
- `.ubsignore` (verify patterns are bandit-compatible)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Running UBS on a project with .ubsignore correctly excludes listed paths from bandit scan
2. `test-suite/` in .ubsignore eliminates test file false positives from bandit output
3. Glob patterns in .ubsignore (e.g., `modules/helpers/*.go`) are correctly handled
4. Other scanners (semgrep, ruff, etc.) continue to work with .ubsignore patterns
5. The filtered workspace approach (rsync) works when rsync is available
6. Fallback to direct -x passing works when rsync is not available
7. Finding count drops significantly (from ~10,879 to expected real findings only)
notes:
## E2E Test

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "=== UBS Bandit .ubsignore E2E Test ==="

# Setup: create temp project with test files
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR/src" "$TMPDIR/test-suite"

# Real code (should be scanned)
cat > "$TMPDIR/src/app.py" << 'PY'
import subprocess
subprocess.call(input("cmd: "), shell=True)  # Should flag: B602
PY

# Test code (should be EXCLUDED)
cat > "$TMPDIR/test-suite/test_app.py" << 'PY'
import subprocess
subprocess.call("echo test", shell=True)  # Should NOT appear
PY

# Create .ubsignore
echo "test-suite/" > "$TMPDIR/.ubsignore"

# Run UBS
echo "[1/3] Running UBS without .ubsignore..."
BEFORE=$(cd "$TMPDIR" && ubs --python --no-ubsignore 2>&1 | grep -c "B602" || echo 0)
echo "  Bandit B602 findings: $BEFORE"

echo "[2/3] Running UBS with .ubsignore..."
AFTER=$(cd "$TMPDIR" && ubs --python 2>&1 | grep -c "B602" || echo 0)
echo "  Bandit B602 findings: $AFTER"

echo "[3/3] Verify reduction..."
if [[ "$AFTER" -lt "$BEFORE" ]]; then
    echo "PASS: .ubsignore reduced findings from $BEFORE to $AFTER"
else
    echo "FAIL: .ubsignore did not reduce bandit findings ($BEFORE -> $AFTER)"
    exit 1
fi
```

title: Epic: Automate toon_rust binary installation in UBS installer
description:
## Overview

The UBS installer (`install.sh`) must automatically download and install the toon_rust `tru` binary as part of the standard installation process. Users should NOT need to manually:
- Download toon_rust
- Build from source
- Set TOON_TRU_BIN/TOON_BIN environment variable
- Configure shell profiles

Everything must be fully automated, just like ast-grep, ripgrep, and jq installations are today.

## Background & Rationale

### Current State
- UBS supports `--format=toon` for ~50% smaller output (optimized for LLM token efficiency)
- TOON encoding uses the toon_rust `tru` binary (Node.js toon CLI is not permitted)
- User must manually set `TOON_TRU_BIN=/path/to/tru` to force the fast Rust version
- This friction means most users miss the fast Rust encoder by default

### Why This Matters
- toon_rust is ~10x faster than the Node.js implementation
- No Node.js runtime dependency required
- Consistent with UBS philosophy: batteries-included, zero-config
- TOON format is critical for AI/LLM workflows where token efficiency matters

### Naming Conflict Issue
- Original toon_rust binary name conflicted with the Unix translate command
- Solution: use the `tru` binary name everywhere and install as `tru` in ~/.local/bin
- UBS already sets `TOON_TRU_BIN`, so the binary name is abstracted away

## Success Criteria
1. Fresh UBS install automatically downloads platform-appropriate toon_rust binary
2. Binary installed to ~/.local/bin/tru (or platform equivalent)
3. TOON_TRU_BIN automatically configured (shell profile or ubs internal default)
4. `ubs --format=toon` works out-of-box with Rust encoder
5. No Node.js fallback (only toon_rust)
6. Works on Linux (x86_64, arm64) and macOS (x86_64, arm64)

## Architecture Notes
- Follow existing patterns from install.sh (see ast-grep, ripgrep, jq downloads)
- Use GitHub releases for binary distribution
- Verify checksums for security
- Support --dry-run for testing

title: Core: Auto-configure TOON_BIN in ubs script
description:
## Task

Modify the ubs script to automatically detect and use the installed `tru` binary without requiring user configuration.

## Current State

```bash
# In ubs script (line ~147)
# TOON_BIN should default to tru (toon_rust); Node `toon` is forbidden
```

## Proposed Change

```bash
# Auto-detect toon_rust binary location (no Node.js fallback)
detect_toon_bin() {
  local candidates=(
    "$HOME/.local/bin/tru"     # Standard install location
    "$HOME/.cargo/bin/tru"     # Cargo install location
    "/usr/local/bin/tru"       # System-wide install
  )
  for bin in "${candidates[@]}"; do
    if [[ -x "$bin" ]]; then
      echo "$bin"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  # Fall back to PATH lookup
  if command -v tru >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v tru
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

# Resolution order: TOON_TRU_BIN > TOON_BIN > tru (PATH)
TOON_BIN="${TOON_TRU_BIN:-${TOON_BIN:-tru}}"
```

## Why This Approach

1. **Zero user configuration** - Works out of box after installation
2. **Respects user override** - TOON_TRU_BIN/TOON_BIN env var still works
3. **No Node.js fallback** - Only toon_rust encoder is accepted
4. **Multiple install locations** - Supports different installation methods

## Location

Modify ubs script near line 147 where TOON_BIN is defined.

## Dependencies

- ultimate_bug_scanner-3a6.4 (Core: integration - binary must be installed first)

## Testing

- Fresh install: should auto-detect ~/.local/bin/tru
- Manual override: TOON_TRU_BIN=/custom/path should work
- Missing tru: should warn and fall back to JSON output (no Node.js)

title: Runner/Installer: ast-grep version compatibility + PATH validation
description:
Problem:
- ubs pins ast-grep 0.40.1 for JS/TS accuracy (tool-cache auto-provision).
- install.sh binary fallback currently downloads ast-grep 0.18.0 and adds it to PATH.
- ubs preflight currently accepts any PATH ast-grep/sg if '--version' contains 'ast-grep' (no capability check).

Impact:
- On systems where installer uses binary fallback (no brew/cargo), users can end up with an old ast-grep in PATH. ubs will then prefer PATH and may break or misbehave if that version lacks required flags/output contracts (e.g. --json=stream/metaVariables) even though tool-cache would have provided the correct pinned build.

Goal:
- Make JS/TS scanning deterministic and reliable: if PATH ast-grep is unusable/outdated, ubs should ignore it and fall back to the verified tool-cache build.
- Align install.sh fallback download to the same pinned version (or at least a compatible minimum) so offline/locked-down users still get a working ast-grep at install time.

Acceptance criteria:
- ubs only uses PATH ast-grep/sg when it passes the same capability checks as doctor (e.g. 'scan -h' and '--json=stream' support as exercised by modules). Otherwise it auto-provisions (or uses) the tool-cache ast-grep 0.40.1.
- install.sh binary fallback for ast-grep downloads a compatible version and (ideally) warns if it can’t verify compatibility.
- Add/adjust a regression test that simulates a bogus/old 'ast-grep' on PATH and ensures ubs selects tool-cache instead.

title: modules/ubs-js.sh: fail fast (env error) instead of regex fallback on TS/TSX
description: When ast-grep isn't usable, the JS module prints 'regex fallback mode' and continues, which can explode into dozens of false positives on TSX/TypeScript syntax. Change default behavior: if TS/TSX/JSX is present and no AST engine is available, stop and return an explicit environment error.

title: JS/TS: fix global-pollution heuristic false positives (JSX props, default params, TS syntax)
description: The 'Global variable assignments' detector in modules/ubs-js.sh uses a regex-based Python heuristic that can misinterpret valid TS/TSX syntax (multiline JSX props and default parameters) as top-level assignments, producing bogus criticals/warnings.

title: JS/TS: AST-confirm high-severity regex findings before reporting
description: Even with ast-grep installed, some UBS JS checks are regex/heuristic-based and can produce false positives on TS/TSX syntax. For the highest-severity findings (CRITICAL/WARNING), add a lightweight AST confirmation step so we only report matches that correspond to real syntax nodes.
notes:
Initial audit:
- Some CRITICAL/WARNING checks in `modules/ubs-js.sh` still use ripgrep regex counts even when ast-grep is available.
- This causes:
  - False positives / miscounts from matches in comments/strings (e.g., `debugger` mentioned in comments).
  - A real coverage gap: the current typeof check only matches `typeof(<expr>)` (paren form) and misses the common `typeof x === 'array'` form used in fixtures.

Implementation plan:
1) Add ast-grep-backed counting + sample output helpers (so high-sev findings show real syntax nodes).
2) Convert at least these high-sev rules to AST when available:
   - Direct NaN comparisons (==/===/!=/!== with NaN on either side)
   - Loose equality (== / != binary expressions)
   - Invalid typeof comparisons (typeof comparisons to invalid string literals; include both paren + non-paren, and handle yoda form)
   - debugger statements (debugger statement node)
3) Add a manifest regression case that ensures invalid typeof comparisons are detected (and not dependent on parenthesized typeof).

title: modules/ubs-js.sh: honor UBS_AST_GREP_BIN for AST engine
description: To enable ubs-level tool caching (and avoid PATH issues), the JS module should accept an explicit ast-grep binary path via env var and use it preferentially when valid.

title: JS/TS: guarantee AST scanning + eliminate TSX regex-fallback false positives
description: When UBS runs on TS/TSX projects it can fall back to regex/heuristic scanning and produce large numbers of false positives (e.g., multiline JSX attributes and default parameters misread as assignments/comparisons). This epic makes JS/TS scanning syntax-aware by default (ast-grep always available/used) and defines a strict degraded-mode policy so we never spam users with bogus CRITICAL/WARNING counts.

title: Spec: JS/TS degraded-mode policy when AST engine is unavailable
description: Define the contract for how UBS behaves when JS/TS scanning cannot use a syntax-aware engine (ast-grep or equivalent). The goal is: never emit large bogus CRITICAL/WARNING counts from regex fallback; treat missing AST as an environment error with clear remediation.

title: JS/TS: inventory TS/TSX false positives + map to scanners
description: Before changing behavior, build a precise map from reported false positives to the exact UBS JS module checks that emitted them (regex/heuristic vs ast-grep). This prevents us from fixing the wrong layer and accidentally reducing real bug coverage.

title: Infra: Set up toon_rust GitHub releases with platform binaries
description:
## Task

Configure toon_rust repository to publish pre-built `tru` binaries for all supported platforms via GitHub releases.

## Required Release Assets

For each release (e.g., v0.1.1), publish:
- `tru-linux-amd64.tar.xz` - Linux AMD64
- `tru-linux-arm64.tar.xz` - Linux ARM64
- `tru-darwin-amd64.tar.xz` - macOS Intel
- `tru-darwin-arm64.tar.xz` - macOS Apple Silicon
- `tru-windows-amd64.zip` - Windows AMD64
- `*.sha256` files for each asset

## Implementation Options

1. **GitHub Actions workflow** (recommended)
   - Cross-compile on release tag push
   - Use `cross` for Linux targets
   - Native build for macOS via matrix

2. **Manual release process**
   - Document build commands for each platform
   - Less ideal but works

## Binary Naming

The binary inside the archive should be named `tru` (not `tr`) to:
- Avoid conflict with Unix `tr` command
- Make purpose clear
- Allow safe PATH inclusion

## Archive Structure

```
tru-linux-amd64.tar.xz
└── tru  (the binary)
```

## Reference

See how ast-grep does releases:
https://github.com/ast-grep/ast-grep/releases

## Dependencies

None - can be done in parallel with other work.

## Notes

This work happens in the toon_rust repository, not ultimate_bug_scanner.
The UBS installer will consume these release assets.

title: Core: Integrate toon_rust installation into main installer flow
description:
## Task

Add toon_rust binary installation to the main installer workflow, making it part of the standard UBS installation process.

## Integration Point

In install.sh, after other binary installations (ast-grep, jq, etc.), add:

```bash
# Install TOON encoder (toon_rust) for fast --format=toon support
install_toon_encoder() {
  local platform arch
  platform="$(detect_platform)"
  arch="$(detect_arch)"
  
  log "Installing TOON encoder (toon_rust)..."
  
  if download_toon_binary "$platform" "$arch"; then
    success "TOON encoder installed to ~/.local/bin/tru"
    # Update TOON_TRU_BIN in ubs script or shell profile
    configure_toon_bin
  else
    warn "TOON encoder installation failed. TOON output will be unavailable until tru is installed."
  fi
}
```

## Call Site

Add to main installation sequence (~line 1200-1300):
```bash
# After install_dependencies()
install_toon_encoder
```

## Conditional Installation

Consider making this optional with a flag:
- `--no-toon` to skip TOON encoder installation
- Default: install it

## Degradation Behavior

If toon_rust installation fails:
1. Log warning (not error)
2. Continue with installation
3. TOON output remains unavailable until tru is installed

## Dependencies

- bd-3a6.3 (Core: download_toon_binary() function must exist)

- Full installation on fresh system

title: Core: Auto-configure TOON_BIN in ubs script
description:
## Task

Modify the ubs script to automatically detect and use the installed `tru` binary without requiring user configuration.

## Current State

```bash
# In ubs script (line ~147)
# TOON_BIN should default to tru (toon_rust); Node `toon` is forbidden
```

## Proposed Change

```bash
# Auto-detect toon_rust binary location (no Node.js fallback)
detect_toon_bin() {
  local candidates=(
    "$HOME/.local/bin/tru"     # Standard install location
    "$HOME/.cargo/bin/tru"     # Cargo install location
    "/usr/local/bin/tru"       # System-wide install
  )
  for bin in "${candidates[@]}"; do
    if [[ -x "$bin" ]]; then
      echo "$bin"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  # Fall back to PATH lookup
  if command -v tru >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v tru
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

# Resolution order: TOON_TRU_BIN > TOON_BIN > tru (PATH)
TOON_BIN="${TOON_TRU_BIN:-${TOON_BIN:-tru}}"
```

## Why This Approach

1. **Zero user configuration** - Works out of box after installation
2. **Respects user override** - TOON_TRU_BIN/TOON_BIN env var still works
3. **No Node.js fallback** - Only toon_rust encoder is accepted
4. **Multiple install locations** - Supports different installation methods

## Location

Modify ubs script near line 147 where TOON_BIN is defined.

## Dependencies

- bd-3a6.4 (Core: integration - binary must be installed first)

## Testing

- Fresh install: should auto-detect ~/.local/bin/tru
- Manual override: TOON_TRU_BIN=/custom/path should work
- Missing tru: should warn and fall back to JSON output (no Node.js)

title: Epic C: Performance program — measure, prefilter, cache, schedule, stream
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Deliver the README's promise for real: `ubs <file>` p95 < 1 s, a 50K-line polyglot repo < 10 s, a 400K-line TypeScript monorepo < 120 s, RSS < 200 MB, zero module timeouts on the benchmark corpus — and prove it continuously with a benchmark job whose regression alarm is statistically sound (CUSUM), not a brittle percentage.

## Measured baseline (this machine, 2026-09-02)
single Python file 5.8 s, single JS file 4.6 s; this repo (15 files) 9.1 s; test-suite tree (514 files, 29K lines, 10 languages) 40 s (~730 lines/s vs README's 10,000+); franchise_location_data_tool --only=python (597 files, 124K lines) 143 s; lumera_ai --only=js (407 files, 407K lines) module timeout at 300 s with 840 MB RSS; meta-runner overhead ≈ 1.7 s per invocation; JS module CPU/wall ≈ 0.18 → process-spawn bound. ## Mechanisms (each is its own bead)
1. Instrumentation (UBS_PROFILE=1) and a benchmark corpus + CI job with CUSUM alarms.
2. Necessary-literal prefilter: for every ast-grep rule and regex pattern extract the literal tokens any match must contain, run ONE ripgrep pass with the literal set to compute per-file rule bitsets, and run ast-grep / core analyzers only on files that can match.

4. Meta-runner overhead ≤ 150 ms for single-file targets.
5. Merkle-keyed incremental cache: per-file findings keyed by content hash under H(engine‖module‖rulepack); per-directory Merkle nodes let whole unchanged subtrees be skipped.
6. LPT scheduler with a cost model (Graham's 4/3 bound) and work-stealing file shards inside a module.

title: C2: Necessary-literal prefilter — one ripgrep pass computes per-file rule bitsets; ast-grep and analyzers run only on files that can match
description:
## What
For every ast-grep rule (from the pack YAML: pattern literals, `kind`-independent identifiers, member names) and every regex-layer pattern, extract the set of literal tokens any match must contain (e.g. eval, innerHTML, .then(, compare_digest, ParseUnverified). Build one literal file per module and run ONE `rg --json -f literals.txt` (Aho–Corasick/regex-set inside ripgrep) over the file list to produce, per file, the bitset of rules whose literal set intersects it. Then invoke ast-grep `scan -c` only on the subset of files with any candidate rule (via --globs or a per-group file list) and pass the bitsets to ubs_core so analyzers skip files with no candidate. title: C4: Merkle-keyed incremental cache — per-file findings replay, whole-subtree skip, atomic writes, hit-rate in profile
description:
## What
Cache root $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ubs/<H(engine‖module checksum‖rulepack hash)>/. Per-file entry keyed by BLAKE2b(file bytes) storing that file's NDJSON findings. Per-directory Merkle node = hash of child names+hashes (taken from `git ls-files -s` blob ids when in a clean git tree, else stat+content hash) so `ubs .` skips entire unchanged subtrees without re-hashing every file. Cross-file analyzers (D6) record their input set; a cached result is invalidated when any input changes. Writes are atomic (temp + rename), reads lock-free; --no-cache disables; profile reports hit-rate; `ubs doctor` reports cache size and offers `--prune-cache`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- test_cache.py: replay is byte-identical to a cold scan; second run on an unchanged corpus ≥ 5× faster; editing one file invalidates exactly that file's entry; rule-pack change invalidates everything; concurrent scans do not corrupt the cache.
